subject: PrivDeploy CI gating & module consistency for terraform/helm/ansible

Subject: Re: Private deployment requirements and gating checklist

Hi Evelyn / Dev,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme Security and Infrastructure want a concise pre-deploy gate for the private deployment (VPC/on-prem pilot). Attached is our requirements doc (attached: acme-reqs-privdeploy.pdf). Topline asks:

- All Terraform modules must be signed and version-pinned; we need a module provenance checklist.
- State must be encrypted and locked; drift detection and plan approvals required.
- Helm charts must have provenance / cosign signatures and a chart linting report.
- Ansible inventories need strict segmentation between control plane and tenant networks.
- KMS/HSM integration for keys and audit logs retained 7+ years.

Can you send a short CI/CD gating proposal (pipeline steps + owners) and a list of the artifacts you'll provide for our audit team? We need to present this to Procurement on Thursday (11/05).

Thanks,
Alex
Acme Corp

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Duran <alex.duran@acme-corp.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment requirements and gating checklist

Alex —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've sketched a minimal gating pipeline and tools we propose for the pilot; attaching a CI snippet (ci-gate-snippet.yml) and a short checklist below. Happy to expand each item into runbook pages.

Proposed CI/CD gating (high-level):
1) Pre-commit checks: terraform fmt, tflint, ansible-lint, helm lint, kubeval.
2) Static policy test: conftest/OPA + policy bundle (policy as code) run against planned tfplan and rendered helm templates.
3) Build & sign: artifact build step that signs terraform module bundles and helm charts (cosign).
4) Plan stage: terraform plan against a sandbox state (remote backend with encryption) and upload plan artifact.
5) Automated policy evaluation: fail fast if conftest/OPA yields denies; post results to PR.
6) Manual approval gate: designated approver(s) in Acme (Procurement/Security) must sign off on PR with plan artifact attached.
7) Canary apply: automated canary apply to isolated namespace/VPC segment with Terratest smoke checks.
8) Full apply: after canary passes and manual approval, run apply with state locking (DynamoDB lock table for S3 backend).
9) Post-deploy verification: automated checks for routes, security groups, NACLs, and egress proxy configuration.

Key infra controls we will include:
- Remote state (S3) encrypted with KMS CMK pinned to org key, DynamoDB locking for concurrency.
- Terraform workspace isolation per-tenant.
- Provider and module version pinning in module registry + signed artifacts.
- Helm chart provenance: cosign signatures + chart provenance index in private chartrepo.
- Image policy: admission controller (Kyverno) enforcing signed images + allowed registries.
- Ansible inventory: environment-separated inventories with role-based variable files; vault-encrypted secrets (HashiCorp Vault).
- Audit logging: all CI actions and API calls forwarded to Acme SIEM; retention policy set to 7 years in staging for audit.

Attached: ci-gate-snippet.yml (simple pipeline stages). We will produce: terraform-modules-v2.zip (signed bundle), helm-charts-lint-report.pdf, ansible-inventory-segmentation.patch, and a short runbook.

If that looks good I'll assign owners and map to the timeline. Proposed owners:
- Dev: terraform modules & signing
- Laura: helm charts and provenance
- Evelyn: CI gates + canary policy

Proposed timeline: pilot artifacts ready by 11/06, on-prem pilot starting week of 11/09.

—Dev

Attachments: ci-gate-snippet.yml
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment requirements and gating checklist

Team —

Thanks Dev, this is a solid starting point. A few additions / clarifications before we share the formal package with Acme and AuditOps:

1) Policy enforcement: make the OPA/conftest policy artifacts part of the module repo (policy bundle v-tagged) and include Conftest results in artifact metadata.
2) Tamper evidence: add provenance metadata to signed terraform module bundles (SHA256 manifest) and upload to our private artifact store.
3) Access control: confirm that the CI approver group maps to Acme SSO SAML groups; we need explicit approvers defined in the PR template.
4) Network topology: prefer TGW in cloud pilot; for on-prem we should provide a BGP/Circuit diagram and a fallback NAT-only plan if BGP cannot be negotiated.
4a) Egress control: all outbound flows should traverse acme-managed egress proxies or an approved NAT egress; list allowed FQDNs in a central lookup table used by the ansible inventory templates.
5) Secrets lifecycle: rotate CMK per 12 months and ensure Vault rotation for short-lived creds; include KMS key policy drafts for legal/audit review.
6) Drift detection: include scheduled Terraform plan runs (nightly) and a notification channel for drift alerts to Acme SecOps.
7) Testing: require Terratest for any module that touches networking or state management. Non-networking modules can have reduced integration coverage but must still pass unit-style validation.

Action items:
- Laura: produce helm chart signing steps + a sample cosign command and chartrepo ACLs.
- Dev: add Conftest policy bundle to repo and wire up policy eval in CI.
- Marissa: consolidate runbook pages and prepare the audit artifacts bundle (signed modules zip + lint report) — target EOD 11/03.
- Soojin: validate post-deploy verification checks (routes, peering, private DNS resolution).

I'll take point on the canary policy and make sure we have a documented rollback. Once Marissa confirms artifacts we can loop in AuditOps and Acme for formal review.

Evelyn
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
